circuit.role: series resistor from VSYS: about 6 mA at 3.5 V, 15 mA at 3.8 V, 27 mA at 4.2 V, 33 mA at 4.4 V (Vf about 3.3 V at these currents)
circuit.page: p4 (Vf 3.2-4.0 V at 700 mA), p5 curve (about 3.2 V at 10 mA, 3.4 V at 100 mA)

supplies.source: VSYS (battery rail); the 3.3 V rail is below the forward voltage
supplies.I_off: 0 (10 uA max reverse leakage at 5 V is not applied)
supplies.rated: 700 mA typ / 1000 mA peak, about 1.8 W optical at 700 mA: this board uses about 3 % of that

logic: UV_EN from a 3.3 V expander pin to the MOSFET gate
placement: Open hole (or fused-silica/acrylic UV-grade window); polycarbonate blocks 365 nm [mem]. Beam 60 deg per the data sheet (JLCPCB's listing says 120 deg for the M code): the hole wall must clear it.
It is the tallest part of the set (2.4-2.85 mm): check the 4.8 mm cavity at its spot.
Point it away from the user, on the far edge; not next to the AS7341 window if fluorescence is to be measured without direct light.
notes: SAFETY (estimate, not from the data sheet): from the curve the output is roughly 2 mW per mA at low current, so 30 mA gives about 60 mW into a 60 deg cone = about 7 W/m2 at 10 cm and 28 W/m2 at 5 cm. The usual UVA limit for unprotected eyes is 10 W/m2 for long exposure (10 kJ/m2 per day). So: default 33 ohm, a firmware time-out, a visible 'UV on' indicator, and never a brighter setting without a hold-to-light key.
Brightness follows the battery voltage (4:1 over the discharge). If constant output is wanted, replace the resistor with a boost-type LED driver; none was selected.
Second source: G3535N1UVS8U06 365NM, C2915611, 327 in stock.
